title: The heart, reviewed

segments.voice: Yesterday: the creed, six things past the eye, taught by a stranger's questions. Your line was six to believe.

At a checkup, the doctor does two things. She looks for what's working: heart rate, breath, strength. And she looks for what's wrong: a fever, a cough, a lump that shouldn't be there. Two lists on one clipboard. The middle of this year did the same with a different organ. One list was the stations, the good things a heart can grow into. The other was the diseases, the things that make a heart sick. Today, both lists, and the one sentence that holds them together.
screen: `TWO LISTS ON ONE CLIPBOARD.` → `WHAT'S WORKING, WHAT'S WRONG.` → `THE SAME CHECKUP FOR THE HEART.`

segments.voice: In Sahih al-Bukhari, in paraphrase, the Prophet, peace be upon him, says there is a lump of flesh in the body: if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. And it is the heart. Everything the year taught about the inner life hangs on that. The stations, one by one: turning back in repentance, watchfulness, taking account of yourself before you're taken to account, not being owned by things, patience, gratitude, trust after effort, contentment, love, and the two wings of fear and hope, with sincerity of intention running through all of them. The diseases: arrogance, which a hadith in Sahih Muslim defines, in paraphrase, as rejecting the truth and looking down on people. Envy. Showing off. Anger. Greed. Backbiting. Lying. Heedlessness, the plain forgetting of Allah in the rush of the day. And despair, the closed door. Al-Ghazali's Revival, which the year opened, has one part on the things that destroy and one part on the things that save. Where it leads: the Qur'an describes a day when wealth and sons are no help, except to the one who comes to Allah with a sound heart, in paraphrase. You first met that phrase on day five hundred seventeen. That's the point of the checkup. Not a perfect score on either list, but a heart brought back, again and again, toward sound.
screen: `IF THE HEART IS SOUND, ALL IS SOUND.` · `THE STATIONS: WHAT A HEART GROWS INTO.` · `THE DISEASES: WHAT MAKES IT SICK.` · `COME WITH A SOUND HEART.`

segments.voice: If you like, place a hand on your chest and ask one question from the first list: where did I show patience, or gratitude, this week? Then one from the second, where did envy, or anger, or showing off slip in, and let a moment come without arguing with it; no verdict, no score. If you pray, turn both moments over to Allah in your own words; and if despair has settled in and won't lift, please reach out: in the US, call or text 988, any hour, or elsewhere, local emergency help.
The heart. Al-qalb, the lump of flesh the hadith says the whole body follows, checked for what it is growing and what is making it sick. Today's word.
Your line: check the heart. Two lists, one heart, brought back again and again. Go gently.

howItsDone: Muslims who follow the inward path read works such as al-Ghazali's Revival of the Religious Sciences, study the virtues and diseases of the heart with a teacher, and take account of themselves at the end of the day.

chat.says: What does Islam mean by a sound heart?
options: A heart that keeps growing in patience and turning back from envy and arrogance.
A heart that has never felt envy or anger even once: a perfect score.
A healthy physical heart; the hadith is really about diet and exercise.
